names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Αγαπητός πάπας Ρώμης», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 17 April, „Св. Агапит папа Римски.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with папа Римски left off: this corpus keeps the see in `office`, where this folder already has Bishop of Rome, and the rank in `types`. The heading gives no epithet beyond the see, so the bare forename is left. Measured, and the reader's prediction was wrong: `corpus-gate.mjs` run without `--batch` lists `? "агапит" — agapitus-of-rome, agapitus-the-deacon`, and `agapitus-the-deacon` holds a bare **Russian** Агапит of the same spelling, so the fold crosses languages and no check of Serbian forms could have seen it. A deliberate fold, recorded in the run's findings.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 17 апреля ст. ст., name page 55, «Святитель Агапит I Римский, папа», with the rank word and the office left off; the day's own line gives the name in the genitive, «Агапита». No folder in this corpus holds this form, and the gate's key for it has no other holder, measured. The regnal number is part of the name the calendar's link gives and is kept; the see is this folder's `office` and is left out of the form.

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Πάπας Αγαπητός πέθανε το 536 στην Κωνσταντινούπολη, ένα χρόνο μετά την ενθρόνιση του», and its heading has «Αγιος Αγαπητος Παπας Ρωμης (; - 536)». The page gives 535 for his election and no year of birth.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 17 апреля ст. ст. — «Свт. Агапита , папы Римского (536).»
source.note: The day's fifth entry. It carries no typikon icon — the day's three stand before the first three entries — so no `rank` is recorded, and none of the day's four hymns is his. The name page behind the line (55) gives «День памяти: 17 апреля» and no other day, and the nominative it carries gives him the regnal number the line does not. Its year, 536, is the one this folder already carries, and the life adds the year of his accession, 535.

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Αγαπητός πάπας Ρώμης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and heads him «(; - 536)». The corpus holds three others whose names fold onto this one — Agapitus of Synnada, Agapitus of the Kyiv Caves and Agapitus the deacon — and none of them is a bishop of Rome. The page prints a couplet but no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.04.2026 (17. април ст. ст.) — „Св. Агапит папа Римски.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, on the same menologion day the Greek keeps him on. **The 536 agrees exactly** with what the folder already holds off saint.gr, so no date was added and none changed. New: that he was **sent by Theodotus, king of the Goths, to the emperor Justinian at Constantinople, to turn him from his campaign against the Goths** — an embassy neither other page read for this folder mentions, where saint.gr sends him over the monophysite heresy; both reasons stand and neither was chosen. The healings on the road, of a mute and of a blind man, are the Greek page's two wonders in the same order, the second of which it places at the Golden Gate of Constantinople rather than on the journey. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
